title: Build hw6 security demo

messages.text:
Generate everything inside hw6/ in this workspace.
Build from the supplied prompts without inspecting other
folders, Git history, or the completed application.

Use Python 3.13. Pin Flask 3.1.3 and Werkzeug 3.1.9.
Put pytest 9.2.0 and ruff 0.17.4 in the dev dependency group.
Create a compatible uv.lock.

Support these commands:
uv sync --locked --group dev
uv run --locked pytest -q
uv run --locked python app.py --demo
uv run --locked python app.py --port 5007

Run the tests and security demo, and fix failures without
weakening the security controls. Report the actual results.

Do not start the web server; I will start it myself.
Do not commit or push anything from this replay workspace.

Do not create any recording script, narration, or speaking
notes file. This overrides Prompt 2's recording-script request.

I’ll check for the supplied prompts at the workspace root and in `hw6/`, then build and verify everything inside `hw6/`. I won’t inspect other folders or Git history, start the server, or commit anything.

I found both prompts in `hw6/prompts.txt`. They specify a local Secure Notes app with private notes, revocable sessions, CSRF protection, rate limiting, and an in-process security demo. I’ll rebuild the source and tests directly from those prompts and omit the recording-script deliverable as requested.

I’ll use opaque session tokens backed by hashed database records so logout can revoke captured cookies. Each POST will require a server-side CSRF token, and each note query will include the owner’s ID. I’m also adding bounded request parsing, authentication rate limits, session storage limits, and loopback host validation.

The app and local interface are in place, and `uv.lock` resolved successfully with the requested pins. I’m now adding tests and the temporary-data demo for note isolation, CSRF, session revocation, malformed input, and rate-limit boundaries. All checks will use Flask’s test client without opening a socket.

The tests now cover hostile inputs and state preservation: rejected edits must leave notes intact, and replayed cookies must fail after logout. I’ve also added concurrent rate-limit checks and tests that inspect the server-start arguments through a fake app, so I can verify port 5007 support without starting the server.

The first run finished with 113 tests passing and six failing. Empty POSTs were rejected with the wrong error status, and rejected Host headers broke the error-page renderer. The IPv6 loopback case also failed. I’ll fix those paths while keeping CSRF and host validation enforced.

All 120 tests now pass, and the security demo passes all 13 in-process checks. Locked sync, lock validation, lint, and formatting checks also pass on Python 3.13.14 with the requested package versions. I’ve saved the command output under `hw6/verification/`; the web server has not been started.

Implemented in [hw6/README.md](</Users/brehonparker/Documents/ChatGPT/New project 2/hw6/README.md>) with Python 3.13, all requested dependency pins, and a compatible `uv.lock`.

Actual results:

- Locked sync and lock validation: passed.
- Pytest: **120 passed**.
- Security demo: **13/13 passed**.
- Ruff lint and formatting: passed.

Command output is saved in `hw6/verification/`. No web server was started, no commits or pushes were made, and no recording script was created.

verification_commands.command:
/bin/zsh -lc 'set -o pipefail
UV_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/.uv-cache" uv run --locked ruff check app.py demo.py tests | tee verification/ruff.txt
UV_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/.uv-cache" uv run --locked ruff format --check app.py demo.py tests | tee verification/format.txt'
